title: Quantile-Led Feature Extraction for Multi-Horizon Predictive Maintenance in Industrial Manufacturing Systems
abstract: In data-driven predictive maintenance (PdM), feature extraction is usually treated as fixed preprocessing: a descriptor set is chosen once and reused while the downstream model or forecasting horizon changes. This paper isolates the representation-learning stage and presents a quantile-led feature-extraction framework based on a dual-stage MLP-QRNN hierarchy. QRNN1 learns a broad ten-quantile conditional distribution for each sensor channel, while skip-connected QRNN2 refines a retained mid-tail quantile set into compact, channel-resolved, distribution-aware features. A fixed thirteen-pipeline ablation spans 1-hour, 70-hour, and 30-day regimes across 72 machines in 9 industrial facilities, with the downstream temporal classifier held fixed within each regime. Increasing the retained mid-tail set from two to four quantiles improves 30- and 60-minute F1-score, reaching 75.92% and 72.44% with attention enabled. The results also show that representations do not transfer reliably beyond their design horizon unless feature capacity, temporal embedding, activation strategy, and sensor breadth are scaled with the forecasting task. The unmodified short-horizon extractor falls to 42.90% F1 at 70 hours, whereas horizon-conditioned extractors reach 60.38% at 70 hours and 79.97% at 30 days. The framework therefore supports treating PdM feature extraction as a horizon-dependent representational stage rather than fixed preprocessing.

title: REFINE: Trajectory Representation Learning via Closed-Loop Transcription -- Extended Version
abstract: Trajectory representation learning underpins a wide range of trajectory analytics tasks; however, most existing self-supervised approaches, whether discriminative or generative, adopt an open-loop paradigm, relying on fixed data augmentations or random masking without feedback, which limits their ability to generalize and scale. We propose REFINE, a simple yet effective Representation lEarning Framework vIa closed-loop traNscription rEfinement for trajectory data. Drawing upon feedback control theory, REFINE tightly couples road-network-aware generative reconstruction with feedback-driven contrastive learning, enabling the model to capture fine-grained local movement semantics and global spatio-temporal dependencies without manually designed augmentation views. We further provide a control-theoretic analysis that establishes convergence guarantees for the proposed closed-loop optimization. Extensive experiments on four real-world datasets demonstrate that REFINE consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods across multiple downstream tasks while remaining computationally efficient and scalable. This paper is an extended version of REFINE: Trajectory Representation Learning via Closed-Loop Transcription, to appear in KDD 2026.

title: iBrain: A Unified Foundation Model Reading the Brain from Surface to Spikes
abstract: Invasive neural recordings provide high-fidelity measurements of brain activity, with signals such as intracranial EEG (iEEG) and intracortical spiking activity capturing neural dynamics at different spatial and temporal scales. Yet existing neural foundation models have largely been developed independently for different invasive recording paradigms, leaving joint pretraining across heterogeneous invasive signals underexplored. In this work, we introduce iBrain, a unified foundation model that jointly learns from iEEG and spiking activity. iBrain employs signal-specific encoders to accommodate their distinct signal characteristics and a shared spatiotemporal Transformer backbone to model dependencies across recording channels and time. We pretrain iBrain on over 7,000 hours of heterogeneous neural recordings using masked signal reconstruction and channel-view alignment, promoting contextual modeling of neural dynamics and robustness across different channels. iBrain consistently outperforms single-signal pretraining baselines and achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmarks. Further experiments demonstrate that iBrain exhibits transferability and data efficiency across diverse recording settings. These results highlight the potential of joint pretraining on heterogeneous invasive neural recordings to support scalable neural modeling and transferable representations across recording settings and downstream tasks.

title: Machine learning-based discrimination of ore-bearing potential in rare-metal pegmatites using muscovite elemental geochemistry
abstract: Muscovite geochemistry records pegmatite evolution and rare-metal enrichment and is widely used in mineral exploration, yet most existing criteria are calibrated to individual deposits or districts. However, whether these geochemical signals remain transferable across independent sources is poorly constrained, particularly in literature-compiled datasets where random analysis-level partitioning can allow source-specific information to enter both training and test sets. Here, we compiled 1,218muscovite analyses from 23 published studies and evaluated multielement geochemical discrimination within a source-aware framework integrating literature-level random-effects meta-analysis, grouped model development using 16 sources published through 2024, and locked independent testing on seven sources published in 2025–2026. Random-effects synthesis revealed recurrent ore-bearing–barren contrasts, with positive pooled effects for Li, Rb, Cs, Ta, Al, and Mn and negative effects for Mg, K, and Fe, but substantial between-literature heterogeneity (I2= 57–94%). Elemental distributions, bivariate diagrams, and principal component analysis further showed systematic compositional shifts accompanied by extensive class overlap. Despite this source heterogeneity and compositional overlap, random forest, extreme gradient boosting, and support vector machine models achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC) values of 0.813–0.846and average precision values of 0.847–0.872on the independent test set, with the support vector machine yielding a balanced accuracy of 0.767and an F1 score of 0.773. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analyses consistently ranked Rb, Cs, and Li among the most influential variables across models, with Nb additionally prominent in the support vector machine, although feature-response patterns remained model dependent. These findings demonstrate that source-aware, multielement muscovite geochemistry can support cross-source screening and sample prioritization in rare-metal pegmatite exploration; model scores should be interpreted as relative rankings of ore-bearing tendency, whereas SHAP-derived response transitions represent model- and data-dependent statistical patterns rather than universal geochemical thresholds, calibrated mineralization probabilities, or estimates of economic resource potential.

title: Benchmark for Evaluating LLM-based Question Answering
abstract: Spatio-Temporal Reasoning Benchmark for LLMs This repository contains a benchmarking framework for evaluating Large Language Models on spatio-temporal reasoning tasks. The benchmark automatically generates evaluation cases from templates and domain scenarios, retrieving ground truth from Wikidata to assess LLM factual correctness and reasoning consistency. What's included: Template-based test case generators for six reasoning tasks: Birthplace Historical Sovereignty (BHS), Countries Organizations Members At Year (COMA), Countries To Cross (CTC), Historical Countries of City (HCC), Presidential Successor (PS), and Sum of Years Person in Role (SYPR) Wikidata SPARQL queries and data extraction scripts for building ground truth Evaluation pipeline with multiple matching strategies (exact string, fuzzy matching, LLM-as-judge) Results and analysis for 4 local LLMs (4B–27B parameters) Use this to: Evaluate your own LLMs on spatio-temporal reasoning Benchmark factual consistency across time and space Compare evaluation metrics (exact vs. fuzzy vs. semantic matching) Extend the framework with additional reasoning tasks Requirements: Python 3.8+, Wikidata SPARQL endpoint access, local LLM inference setup

title: Adaptive Noise Injection for Deep Learning with Limited Data
abstract: Deep learning's success hinges on large datasets, a resource frequently lacking in real-world scenarios. This paper proposes an adaptive noise injection technique designed to mitigate overfitting and enhance generalization performance when training deep neural networks with limited labeled data. The core idea involves dynamically adjusting the noise level introduced during training, responding to the model's learning progress and the quantity of available data. We explore different noise injection methods – input noise and parameter noise – and demonstrate their effectiveness through a theoretical framework and illustrative examples. The adaptive nature of this approach allows the model to better capture underlying patterns, avoiding overfitting to noisy or sparse training data. The paper provides a systematic approach to incorporating noise into deep learning models, offering a practical solution for low-data regimes. We analyze the impact of varying noise levels and injection strategies, revealing key insights into optimizing model performance in constrained environments.

title: Non-Linear Topology for Quantum State Generation
abstract: This paper investigates the application of non-linear topology in quantum state generation, focusing on the creation of complex quantum states and enhanced quantum information processing efficiency. We explore a novel dynamic topology approach to generate quantum systems with intricate states, offering a significant advancement over static generation methodologies. The core mechanism utilizes the inherent properties of dynamic topology to construct quantum states with unprecedented complexity. This research demonstrates the potential of this approach to dramatically improve quantum information handling capabilities. The paper presents a detailed analysis of the algorithm, its computational complexity, and preliminary results illustrating the generated quantum states. Finally, the work explores the future directions and potential applications of this technique.

title: Decomposition of Neural Networks via Symbolic Regression
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to understanding and potentially optimizing neural networks by leveraging symbolic regression. The core idea is that a neural network's complex behavior can be represented as a simpler, interpretable symbolic expression. We propose using symbolic regression techniques to identify the underlying mathematical relationships driving the activation patterns within a neural network. This decomposition offers a pathway to improved interpretability and, theoretically, reduced computational requirements. The research investigates the feasibility of this decomposition and presents a framework for applying symbolic regression to neural network analysis. While experimental validation is not included in this theoretical exploration, the framework lays the groundwork for future research and potential practical applications.

title: ##混沌几何的自适应矩阵学习
abstract: This paper introduces a novel method for matrix learning based on the principles of chaotic systems. We propose a "混沌几何自适应矩阵学习" approach that dynamically adjusts the weights of a matrix using an iterative process inspired by the dynamics of chaotic systems. This method aims to achieve high-precision matrix learning by adapting to the inherent instability and complexity of the input data. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulations and analysis, highlighting its ability to surpass traditional matrix learning techniques in terms of accuracy and robustness.

title: Quantum Entanglement and Non-Linear Integral Computation
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, offers a unique pathway to computation, particularly in the realm of complex mathematical functions. This paper explores the development of a novel non-linear integral calculation method leveraging quantum entanglement, aiming to surpass the limitations of traditional methods and achieve significantly enhanced precision. The core mechanism centers on utilizing entangled states to represent and manipulate integral values, thereby streamlining the computation process. The paper details the methodology, highlights the advantages over classical approaches, and concludes with a discussion of the potential implications for various mathematical applications.

title: Quantum Clock Geometry Topology Transformation
abstract: Quantum clock geometry topology transformation is a novel approach to enhancing the precision and controllability of quantum clocks. This research explores the application of geometric topology transformations to the design and implementation of quantum clock algorithms. The core claim is to establish a quantum clock algorithm that leverages geometric topology transformations for precise control and optimization. This work presents a theoretical framework and initial implementation demonstrating the potential for significant improvements in the accuracy and robustness of quantum clock systems. The paper details the mathematical foundations of the proposed transformation, outlines the algorithm's architecture, and presents preliminary results showcasing the efficacy of the technique.

title: Symbolic Regression with Neural Symbolic Networks
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to symbolic regression, termed Neural Symbolic Networks (NSNs), designed to overcome the limitations of traditional neural networks in representing complex mathematical relationships. The core idea is to integrate the strengths of both neural networks and symbolic regression techniques. Neural networks excel at pattern recognition and function approximation, while symbolic regression is specifically designed for discovering mathematical equations from data. NSNs leverage neural networks to learn the initial parameters and structure of symbolic regression systems, which then iteratively refine these parameters to discover accurate mathematical expressions. The system is trained using a combination of gradient descent and a symbolic refinement process. We demonstrate that NSNs can effectively discover complex equations from datasets that are often challenging for standard neural network-based approaches. This approach addresses the core challenge of accurately representing mathematical relationships and offers a promising direction for automated equation discovery and scientific exploration.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Encoding: A Dynamic Adaptive Quantum Bit
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental aspect of quantum mechanics, offers the potential for unprecedented information encoding capabilities. This paper explores the design and application of a dynamic adaptive quantum bit (qubit) encoding protocol leveraging the inherent self-adjusting nature of entangled states. We propose a novel quantum architecture incorporating dynamic entanglement generation and measurement, enabling information storage, transmission, and processing with enhanced redundancy, robustness against interference, and the ability to adapt to environmental changes. This research focuses on the implementation of a quantum-based encoding scheme that surpasses current static approaches, presenting a promising avenue for advanced quantum information processing.

title: 基于量子自适应的计算图设计
abstract: This paper introduces a novel computational graph design leveraging quantum self-adaptivity. Traditional computational graph design relies heavily on static parameter settings, which often struggles to effectively handle dynamic system characteristics. We propose a new approach that dynamically adjusts quantum states based on the system's evolution, leading to improved efficiency and accuracy. This system utilizes quantum self-adaptivity to create a responsive and adaptable graph structure. The paper details the core mechanism of this design, outlining the algorithm for parameter optimization and its impact on computational performance. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations and provide a preliminary analysis of its potential applications. The core claim highlights the significant improvement in computational efficiency and accuracy achieved by this design compared to traditional methods.

title: Dynamic Bayesian Network-Based Dynamic Probability Models
abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic Bayesian network (DBN) based model for probabilistic inference and parameter estimation. Traditional probabilistic models often require manual parameter adjustment, which can be time-consuming and limit the model's flexibility. Our proposed model leverages graph neural networks (GNNs) to dynamically update probability distributions, enabling the automatic learning and adaptation to high-dimensional and dynamic probability spaces. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through several experimental results, showcasing its ability to handle complex scenarios and achieve superior performance compared to existing methods. The core mechanism utilizes GNNs to represent the probability space as a graph, allowing for efficient learning of dependencies and automatic updating of node and edge weights.

title: Quantum Neural Networks Utilizing Measurement-Based Quantum Computation
abstract: This paper explores the potential of utilizing measurement-based quantum computation (MBQC) to accelerate the training of quantum neural networks (QNNs). Traditional QNN training is computationally expensive, posing a significant barrier to their practical implementation. We propose a novel architecture for a QNN that directly employs MBQC principles to perform key calculations involved in the training process. The core idea is to transform the training objective into a series of measurements performed on a quantum state prepared according to the network's parameters. This approach aims to circumvent the limitations of classical optimization algorithms by exploiting quantum superposition and interference. We present a theoretical framework outlining this method, detailing the mapping of the training problem onto a MBQC protocol. The expected speedup, based on the inherent parallelism of MBQC, is discussed, along with potential challenges and future research directions. Specifically, we examine how the measurement process itself can be optimized to reduce noise and improve the accuracy of the trained network. The ultimate goal is to demonstrate a practical approach to training QNNs that leverages the advantages of quantum computation.

title: Dynamic Quantum Geometry Transformation (DQGT)
abstract: This paper introduces Dynamic Quantum Geometry Transformation (DQGT), a novel computational framework that leverages quantum geometry transformations to achieve high-precision, high-efficiency geometric modeling and transformations. The core mechanism centers on the dynamic adjustment of geometric transformation parameters through an algorithm, offering a significant advancement over traditional methods. This advancement promises improved modeling efficiency and accuracy, with potential applications in quantum information storage and transmission.

title: MuJoCo-Based Sim-to-Real Reinforcement Learning for Transition Control of a Triple Inverted Pendulum
abstract: This study presents an experimentally validated MuJoCo-based sim-to-real reinforcement learning framework for transition control among all eight equilibrium points (EPs) of a physical triple inverted pendulum (TIP). A multibody model is constructed from the apparatus properties, and uncertain actuation, damping, and friction parameters are identified by matching measured and simulated trajectories using the covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy. The resulting effective parameter sets are sampled during training using truncated quantile critics to reduce policy dependence on a single model. The trained policies are transferred to the physical TIP without additional tuning or calibration. In the EP0-to-EP7 experiment, the policy trained without parameter identification failed in all ten trials, whereas the policy trained with the identified parameter sets succeeded in all ten. In the sequential experiment, all eight transitions were completed in each of ten trials, yielding 80 successful transitions with no observed failures while satisfying the cart travel and tangential force limits. These results demonstrate sim-to-real transition control across all eight EPs without state resets or precomputed trajectories.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Marketing: A Data-Driven Study of Consumer Purchase Intention
abstract: The present study investigates the effects of artificial intelligence (AI) on consumer purchase intention in a digital marketing environment. As AI-powered technologies become an integral part of marketing, it has been essential for marketers to know how consumers make decisions. This is approached with the empirical view utilizing primary data collected from 598 online consumers across India using purposive sampling. Logistic regression was performed to analyze the data Due to this access, we were able to examine the impact of demographic factors and AI awareness on purchase intention. The results show that demographics such as age, gender and education do not play a role in the intention to purchase in AI-sembedded environments. AI awareness has a positive correlation with purchase intention, but the effect is not statistically significant. These findings indicate traditional demographic segmentations may become less relevant with more AI in the marketing mix and experiential and psychological factors may take center stage.This research adds to the growing body of literature regarding AI in marketing through demonstrated complexity within consumer behavior when mediated through digital platforms and creates new pathways for future exploration by incorporating variables centred on psychological factors and trust.

title: Quantum Computing: Revolutionizing Drug Discovery and Battery Development
abstract: Quantum computing promises to be a game changer for drug discovery and battery development as it will enable simulations of complex molecular and material systems not possible in classical regimes. Here, we introduce a hardware-aware, hybrid quantum-classical framework designed for practical pharmaceutical and energy problems. Extending state-of-the-art results from quantum machine learning, quantum-inspired optimization, and domain-specific datasets, the model improves both scalability and accuracy as well as interpretability. The proposed method is validated from real-drug and battery chemistry with advantages over the traditional method. This interdisciplinary breakthrough tackles major drawbacks of current quantum approaches and provides a realistic pathway towards industrial implementation in chemistry-led innovation.

title: Targeted service improvement for individualized providers
abstract: Online reviews offer valuable insights for service improvement, especially with the increasing availability of multimodal data (e.g., text and images). However, most existing research has primarily focused on industry- or group-level analyses, often overlooking individual business contexts (e.g., performance and competition), the interaction effects between different service attributes, and the full potential of image information. This study fills these gaps by developing a novel multimodal framework that leverages machine learning and optimization theory to generate targeted service improvement recommendations for individual service providers. The three-stage framework begins with extracting and clustering aspect-opinion pairs from review texts and matching them with corresponding image features. Subsequently, we use a feature distribution smoothing-based Bayesian iterative algorithm to address biases from data imbalance and estimate attribute-level interaction effects. Finally, we construct an interaction effect network, propose a probability-based stepwise optimization algorithm, and integrate image features with large language models to generate specific and actionable recommendations for individual providers. Through a large-scale case study of hotel service improvement, we validate the effectiveness of the proposed framework and demonstrate enhanced predictive accuracy and management insights. A user study with practitioners showed that our method outperformed the best baseline by 19.5 % in practitioner satisfaction.

title: FedPerKD privacy aware personalized federated learning with knowledge distillation for edge oriented tomato leaf disease detection
abstract: Abstract Tomato leaf diseases threaten global food security by reducing crop yield and quality. Centralized deep-learning detectors require farms to share raw images, which raises privacy, bandwidth, and data-sovereignty concerns. We present FedPer-KD, a privacy-aware federated framework that combines personalization with client-side knowledge distillation: each client keeps its raw images and personalized classifier head locally while the shared MobileNet-V2 feature extractor is aggregated, and a local EfficientNet-B0 teacher supervises the student through softened logits. We evaluate on the PlantVillage tomato leaf dataset (18,345 images, ten classes) using simulated federated clients ( N = 2, 4, 6) trained for 10, 20, and 30 rounds with five random seeds. FedPer-KD reaches 99.34% test accuracy and 99.33% macro-F1 at six clients and 20 rounds while transmitting only the shared base (~ 8.9 MB per client per round, a 36% saving over FedAvg on the same student). Across 2–6 clients it consistently outperforms FedAvg, FedProx, Scaffold, FedPer, FedAvg + KD, and a capacity-matched FedAvg baseline; paired statistical comparisons with Holm-Bonferroni correction confirm significance ( p < 0.05) and Cohen’s d > 1.0 on every comparison. We also report ablations over the Dirichlet heterogeneity parameter (alpha = 0.5, 0.3, 0.1), the teacher fine-tuning schedule, the distillation temperature tau and weight alpha, and a battery of synthetic image corruptions. The framework is privacy-aware rather than formally privacy-preserving, is effective under mild client heterogeneity, and is edge-oriented for downstream deployment.

title: A New Perspective on Clustering: A Mixed-norm Model and its Solution by Progressive Integer Programming
abstract: Extending the classical $K$-means and $K$-medians models, this paper introduces an $\ell_{p,q}$ mixed-norm clustering model where the centroid updates and cluster assignments are under the $\ell_p$ and $\ell_q$ norms, respectively. The model is formulated as a mixed-integer program (MIP) with Heaviside composite constraints that describe the nearest-center assignments. The framework recovers $K$-means and $K$-medians when $p=q=2$ and $p=q=1$, respectively, and yields new models when $p\ne q$. To address the computational challenges, we develop a progressive integer programming (PIP) method that adaptively fixes confident assignments and solves restricted mixed-integer subproblems. For $q=1$, we develop a convex inner approximation of the difference-of-convex constraints in the restricted subproblems, for which a global solution can be computed. Importantly, we establish the connection between the local minimizer and the strong center-local minimizer of the mixed-norm clustering problem and the global optimal solution of the restricted subproblems under certain assumptions. This connection provides a practical certificate of a local minimizer of the nonconvex mixed-norm clustering model. We further develop techniques for constructing adaptive fixing sets and working sets for $q=1$. Extensive numerical experiments demonstrate the superior performance of the mixed-norm clustering model and the efficiency of PIP for solving the MIP model, which may be intractable otherwise. In particular, the $\ell_{2,1}$ mixed-norm clustering model is effective under coordinate-sparse, mean-balanced contamination, whereas the $\ell_{1,2}$ model is preferred under dense coordinatewise Cauchy contamination. The numerical results also show that PIP can escape poor alternating solutions and obtain substantially better feasible clustering, while preserving strong warm starts when no improvement is found.

title: Latent-MoE: Domain-Aware Mixture-of-Experts for PDEs with Multi-Regime Physics
abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) struggle on PDEs whose governing physics varies across the domain. We trace this to a structural property of standard coordinate networks: their neural tangent kernel (NTK) is translation-variant and lets training points of large coordinate magnitude disproportionately influence predictions elsewhere, producing long-range coupling and gradient conflict during training. We show analytically and empirically that mixture-of-experts (MoE) architectures with centered, compact-support routers yield a uniformly banded NTK whose kernel-regression weights decay exponentially with distance, localizing the learning. Building on this, we propose \emph{Latent-MoE}, which interleaves domain-aware MoE blocks within a shared backbone. Unlike FB-PINNs or X-PINNs, which rigidly partition both the domain and the parameters so that the parameters on different subdomains are updated independently, Latent-MoE is designed to preserve the localization benefit of domain-aware routing while allowing capacity to flow across regions through the shared backbone. On standard homogeneous-physics benchmarks Latent-MoE is competitive with established baselines; on benchmarks with multi-stage time-variable physics, where global models and rigid domain decompositions both fall into spurious solutions, it improves over them by more than an order of magnitude, with markedly reduced gradient conflict during training.

title: Agentic Algorithm Engineering: Improving Shared-Memory Exact Minimum Cuts
abstract: The minimum cut problem for an undirected edge-weighted graph asks us to divide its set of nodes into two blocks while minimizing the weighted sum of the cut edges. Over the last years, we engineered a range of fast algorithms for this problem. Our fastest exact algorithm uses an inexact algorithm to obtain a better bound for the problem, reductions that depend on this bound, improved data structures and parallel contraction routines. It is available in the open-source package VieCut and, on real-world instances, outperformed the previously fastest solvers by a factor of up to 2.5 sequentially and up to 12.9 when run in parallel. We improve this algorithm using agentic algorithm engineering (AAE), a methodology that we introduce here, in which autonomous large language model agents run the algorithm engineering cycle on an existing code base: they form hypotheses about where running time is lost, implement them, benchmark the result on a fixed instance set and keep or discard the change. Even though we had already tuned our algorithm by hand extensively, the agent finds significant optimizations, in particular on the DIMACS core instances: factors of 1.28 (sequential) and 1.63 (32 threads) on real-world k-cores, and 6.26 and 127 on the DIMACS core instances.

title: MSSP: Multi-Scale Spatially-Constrained Partition for Unsupervised Semantic Segmentation of 3D Point Clouds
abstract: 3D point cloud semantic segmentation is essential for real-world spatial understanding, yet the prohibitive cost of human annotations motivates unsupervised approaches that require no labels. Existing superpoint-based methods typically rely on spectral analysis at a fixed granularity, failing to capture the hierarchical semantic structures inherent in complex indoor scenes. To bridge this gap, we present a Multi-Scale Spatially-Constrained Partition (MSSP) framework that combines multi-scale spectral analysis with spatially-constrained clustering. Multi-scale spectral analysis constructs enriched superpoint descriptors across multiple clustering granularities; however, the resulting high-dimensional feature space calls for a structural prior to translate into cleaner segmentation. Spatially-constrained clustering supplies this prior by restricting superpoint merging to physically adjacent regions, imposing the spatial coherence needed for multi-scale features to be effective. Extensive experiments on S3DIS and ScanNet show that MSSP achieves the best mIoU among unsupervised methods on the main benchmarks, with particularly significant gains on S3DIS. Notably, our ablation reveals a regularize-then-enrich interaction: multi-scale features alone do not improve final segmentation, yet become highly effective when coupled with spatial regularization, underscoring that spatial coherence is aprerequisite for multi-scale representations in superpoint clustering.

title: [Artifact] Redefining Grey-Box Deobfuscation through Context-Aware Program Synthesis, and Application to MBA
abstract: Redefining Grey-Box Deobfuscation: Context-Aware Program Synthesis at Scale, and Application to MBA This is the artifact for the CCS'26 publication, "Redefining Grey-Box Deobfuscation: Context-Aware Program Synthesis at Scale, and Application to MBA" We propose in this artifact to replay the Tables 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 of the paper, namely 2 - Evaluation of GreySynth against competitors on ProMBA and C datasets3 - Scalability analysis of GreySynth against competition on C-MBA dataset4 - Ablation study of Global vs OES vs CHS5 - Impact of constant values injection6 - Impact of the internal synthesizer We provide the source in OCaml for further inspection from the reviewers, not just binaries. Installation The artifact ships as a Docker image `tar` archive inside the Zenodo record. All tools and datasets are already built into the image; nothing is fetched from a private repo or server. Only one external image (ProMBA) is pulled from a public registry to evaluate that competitor. Download the record from Zenodo, then run the following commands: 1. Pull the ProMBA competitor image (required to evaluate ProMBA, see below): `docker pull astean1001/promba:v1` 2. Import the GreySynth image from the archive shipped in the record: `docker load -i greysynth.tar` 3. Create and enter a container, sharing the Docker socket: `docker run -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock --name greysynth -it greysynth` Add `-m 8g --cpuset-cpus=0-7` to cap the container at 8GB of memory and cores 0-7 (8 cores). 4. To get back into the container after exiting: `docker start -i greysynth` Sharing the Docker socket (`-v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock`) is mandatory to evaluate the ProMBA competitor. Use We have set up scripts to replay the whole tables, which can be run by `python scripts/tables/run_table_2.py` to replay Table 2, and likewise `run_table_3.py` ... `run_table_6.py`. Each table has a companion layout file `scripts/tables/table_X.layout`, a JSON file that lets you change parameters and/or deactivate tools or configurations. All layouts share `timeout` (time budget per expression) and `limit` (number of randomly sampled expressions per dataset). Per table: - **Table 2**: `tools` (`syntia`, `xyntia`, `xsmir`, `qsynth`, `promba`, `gamba`, `greysynth`) and `datasets` (`synthetic_mba`, `mba_loki`, `c_mba#omvll`, `c_mba#mba_obfuscator`, `c_mba#tigress_lvl_5`, `c_beyond_mba#omvll`, `c_beyond_mba#tigress_lvl_5`).- **Table 3**: `tools` and `datasets`.- **Table 4**: `cache` (a *list* of caching values, see §5.5) and `configs` (a list of configurations toggling `global`, `oes`, `chs`).- **Table 5**: `injecting_constants` (inject constants identified in the AST) and `synthesizers` (`xyntia`, `xsmir`).- **Table 6**: `synthesizers` (adds `cvc5` and `syntia`) and `internal_timeouts` (GreySynth's internal synthesizer timeout). Repurposing GreySynth on your own expressions Beyond replaying the tables, GreySynth can simplify arbitrary obfuscated expressions of your own. The `greysynth` binary is on the container's `PATH`. ## Calling conventionGreySynth takes an obfuscated expression (`-obf`), an optional ground-truth reference (`-gt`) used only for quality metrics, and a config JSON file as the single positional argument: ```greysynth -obf -string " " [-gt -string " "] greysynth -obf -cil [-gt -cil ] ``` The obfuscated and ground-truth sources can be mixed freely, e.g. `-obf -cil obf.c target -gt -string "x + y" config.json`. Two ways to provide an expression: - **`-string " "`** — a raw expression in DBA syntax. Variables carry an explicit bit size in angle brackets, e.g. `x<64>`. Supported operators: arithmetic (`+ - * / %`), bitwise (`& | ^ ~`), shifts (`<< >> >>s`), rotates (`rol ror`), comparisons (`== != < <= > >=`), extensions (`uext(n)`, `sext(n)`) and restriction (`restrict(lo, hi)`). Example: ``` greysynth -obf -string "(x<64> & y<64>) + (x<64> | y<64>)" default.json ``` (`-string-file ` reads the same syntax from a file.) - **`-cil `** — a C file plus a function name. GreySynth extracts and simplifies the return expression of that function. The function's parameters become the expression's variables. Example, given `obf.c` containing `int64_t target(int64_t x, int64_t y) { return (x & y) + (x | y); }`: ``` greysynth -obf -cil obf.c target default.json ``` Add `-size ` to set the default bit width for variables that don't carry an explicit ` ` suffix. Config JSON Key Type Meaning oes bool Enable the OES core component (Section 5). global_synthesis bool Attempt global synthesis at each node. local_synthesis bool Attempt local synthesis at each node (the local, context-aware path). local_cache bool Cache synthesis results across nodes (Section 5.5). synthesizer string Internal synthesis engine: `"xyntia"`, `"syntia"` or `"cvc5"`. synthesis_timeout int Per-synthesis-call timeout, in seconds. total_timeout int Overall time budget for one expression, in seconds. nb_samples int Number of I/O samples used to drive black-box synthesis. add_constants_to_synthesis bool Inject constants found in the AST into synthesis (Table 5). xsmir_ops string Extra operator set passed to the XSmir backend (empty for the default set). The last argument is a JSON file describing GreySynth's parameters. A ready-to-use `default.json` ships in the container; copy and edit it. The most useful keys: We join a `greysynth.json` example for the config JSON file.

title: Modeling and Analytical Characterization of Neuronal Networks Constructed from Reservoir Computing Based Model
abstract: Introduction Electrophysiological studies in neuroscience probe interactions among neuronal populations across multiple scales, from single-cell activity to large network dynamics [1,2]. Here, we present a computational framework to decode signals from microelectrode array (MEA) recordings [3]. The model is based on Reservoir Computing (RC) and learns spike-rate sequences to reproduce network responses to external stimuli. A key outcome is a macroscopic connectivity map capturing effective connectivity with higher accuracy than standard statistical methods such as cross-correlation and transfer entropy. We describe the model, discuss its implications and limitations, and present applications to cultured neuronal networks under different interventions. Methods The approach relies on electrophysiological recordings from mouse cortical cultures acquired via microelectrode arrays (MEA). After preprocessing (filtering and spike detection), signals are converted into multichannel instantaneous spike-rate (ISR) sequences, from which bursting episodes are extracted. These are used to train an artificial neural network with a reservoir computing (RC) architecture to learn the synaptic transmission function underlying rate-coded activity. The network is represented macroscopically, with nodes corresponding to MEA electrodes. The RC reservoir performs nonlinear transformations with leaky memory, and outputs are obtained via LASSO-regularized linear regression [4]. Results Model validation followed two complementary approaches. First, the inferred connectivity map was benchmarked against a ground-truth network generated in silico, with simulations designed to replicate MEA measurements. Second, both in silico and in vitro (real neuronal cultures) data were used in a predictive framework: the model was trained and validated on spontaneous activity, while testing was performed using responses to controlled local stimuli, including optogenetic perturbations. Model predictions under identical stimuli were then compared with the recorded responses. In the presentation, we will report the model's performance and highlight selected applications along with their results. Discussion In this study, we developed a computational model that decodes spatio-temporal data from electrophysiological measurements of neuronal cultures. The model reconstructs the network structure on a macroscopic domain and predicts the response to a localized stimulus. Our primary goal was to create an advanced experimental data analysis tool for processing complex time-series. The results obtained indicate that the model not only serves as a data analyzer but can also function as a network simulator. title: Autonomous Theorem Proving via Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Automated theorem proving (ATP) has long been a central goal in artificial intelligence, aiming to create systems capable of automatically generating mathematical proofs. However, current ATP systems often suffer from brittleness, requiring extensive manual tuning and intervention from human experts. This paper proposes a novel approach to autonomous theorem proving leveraging hierarchical reinforcement learning (HRL). Our core idea is to train an agent that learns to decompose complex theorems into smaller, more manageable subgoals and dynamically select appropriate proof strategies. This hierarchical structure allows the agent to explore the proof space more efficiently and adapt to different theorem types. We formulate the theorem proving process as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) and utilize HRL to learn an optimal policy. The learned policy is represented as a tree structure, where each node represents a subgoal and the edges represent possible proof steps. We evaluate the approach on a suite of mathematical problems and demonstrate its potential for significant improvements in robustness and automation. The primary contributions of this work lie in the integration of HRL with ATP and the development of a hierarchical representation for proof strategies.

title: Quantum Machine Learning: A Novel Approach to Variable Tensor & Activation Function
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) is a rapidly evolving field exploring the potential of quantum computing to revolutionize machine learning. This paper introduces a novel quantum machine learning algorithm, termed "Variable Tensor & Activation Function" (VTAF), which leverages the unique properties of variable tensors and activation functions to enhance data representation and improve machine learning performance. We propose a new algorithm architecture based on the integration of these components, aiming to overcome limitations of existing quantum machine learning approaches. The core claim of this work is that VTAF can effectively capture complex relationships within data, resulting in improved performance across a range of machine learning tasks. The algorithm's design incorporates quantum entanglement and superposition to facilitate the exploration of high-dimensional spaces, leading to enhanced feature extraction and pattern recognition. We detail the algorithm's architecture, demonstrate its effectiveness through illustrative examples, and discuss potential future research directions.

title: Physical Physics Simulation of Quantum Entanglement-Driven Computation
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of quantum entanglement as a key component in accelerating physical simulation calculations. Traditional computational methods often struggle with the inherent complexity and exponential scaling of simulating quantum systems. We propose a novel framework, leveraging the unique properties of entanglement, to overcome these limitations. This framework utilizes entanglement to facilitate efficient quantum computations, offering the prospect of vastly improved simulation speeds and the ability to model more intricate quantum systems. The core mechanism focuses on optimizing quantum algorithms through entanglement manipulation, specifically targeting key challenges in simulating complex quantum phenomena. This research explores the practical implications of this approach, providing a theoretical foundation and a potential pathway toward revolutionizing the field of physical simulation.

title: Self-Adapting Quantum Topology Models: A Novel Approach to Complex Quantum System Simulation
abstract: Quantum topology, a rapidly developing field, promises revolutionary advancements in quantum information processing and computation. However, creating and simulating complex quantum systems remains a significant challenge. This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum system simulation, leveraging self-adaptive algorithms to generate highly accurate and scalable models. We propose a model that dynamically adjusts parameters to effectively represent the intricate dynamics of quantum systems, overcoming limitations of traditional methods. The core mechanism involves a hierarchical, self-organizing structure that facilitates the exploration of complex quantum landscapes. This approach offers significant advantages in terms of computational efficiency and the ability to handle intricate quantum phenomena. The model's potential applications span diverse fields, including quantum materials, quantum optics, and fundamental physics. We demonstrate the efficacy of this self-adaptive model through a series of numerical simulations, showcasing its capacity to capture crucial aspects of complex quantum behavior.

title: 基于量子纠缠的自适应拓扑变换算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive topology transformation algorithm based on quantum entanglement. The algorithm leverages the unique properties of entangled states to perform highly precise and efficient topological transformations, offering significant improvements in computational speed and information processing capabilities compared to existing methods. We explore the potential of this approach for both quantum computation and quantum information processing, focusing on enhancing the performance of critical operations. The core mechanism involves manipulating entangled states to induce topological changes, achieving a significant reduction in computational complexity and enhancing the fidelity of the resulting topological structures. This research aims to provide a robust and efficient tool for tackling complex topological problems.

title: Probabilistic Logic Programming with Bayesian Uncertainty
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to programming known as Probabilistic Logic Programming, which seeks to bridge the gap between the deductive strength of logic programming and the expressive power of Bayesian networks. The core idea is to develop a logic programming language that inherently supports Bayesian inference, allowing for the representation and manipulation of probabilistic knowledge within a logical framework. This is achieved through a mechanism that integrates probabilistic rules with logical constraints, enabling the system to reason under uncertainty. The proposed system addresses limitations of existing approaches by providing a more natural and intuitive way to represent and reason with incomplete or uncertain information. The paper outlines the fundamental concepts, syntax, and semantics of this new paradigm, highlighting its potential applications in areas such as expert systems, diagnostic reasoning, and decision support systems. The key contribution lies in providing a unified framework for both deterministic and probabilistic deduction, offering a more robust and flexible solution for complex reasoning problems. The system is designed to be both computationally efficient and expressive, allowing for the representation of intricate probabilistic relationships.

title: Non-Linear Matrix Operations: A Quantum Simulation Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum simulation algorithm for non-linear matrix operations, leveraging quantum entanglement to achieve significant computational speedups. We propose a quantum algorithm that utilizes entanglement to accelerate matrix multiplication and addition, moving beyond the limitations of classical approaches. The core mechanism centers on harnessing the unique properties of quantum entanglement to represent and manipulate the matrix transformations, enabling parallel computation and potentially offering a new paradigm for numerical computation. The proposed algorithm demonstrates promising results in simulating certain matrix operations, showcasing the potential for exponential speedups in specific scenarios. This work contributes to the exploration of quantum algorithms for computationally intensive tasks and establishes a foundation for future advancements in quantum simulation.

title: Adaptive Curriculum Learning for Reinforcement Learning via Graph Representations of Tasks
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has achieved remarkable success in various domains, but its application to complex, real-world tasks remains a significant challenge. A primary obstacle is the difficulty of exploration, where agents initially struggle to identify optimal strategies within vast state spaces. This paper proposes a novel approach, Adaptive Curriculum Learning (ACL) for RL, utilizing graph representations of tasks to mitigate this issue. We represent tasks as graphs, where nodes represent states and edges represent transitions, allowing us to quantify task complexity through graph-based metrics. An adaptive curriculum learning algorithm dynamically adjusts the task difficulty based on the agent's performance, guided by these metrics. This approach enables a more efficient learning process by progressively introducing increasingly complex tasks, leading to improved sample efficiency and overall performance. The core contribution lies in the integration of graph representations with adaptive curriculum learning, providing a structured and scalable framework for tackling complex RL problems. We define the following key notations: $S = \{s_1, s_2, ..., s_N\}$ representing the set of states, $A = \{a_1, a_2, ..., a_M\}$ representing the set of actions, $R(s, a) = r_{sa}$ representing the reward function, $P(s, a)$ representing the transition probability, $\gamma \in [0, 1]$ representing the discount factor, $\tau \in \{1, 2, ..., K\}$ representing the curriculum level, $g(s)$ representing the graph-based difficulty metric for state $s$, and $Q(s, a; \tau)$ representing the Q-value for state $s$ and action $a$ at curriculum level $\tau$.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Constraint Satisfaction Problem (CSP) Solving
abstract: Quantum-enhanced constraint satisfaction problem (CSP) solving represents a significant advancement in computational power, potentially enabling the efficient solution of complex optimization problems. This paper investigates the application of quantum annealing and quantum approximate optimization algorithms (QAOA) to tackle CSPs, aiming to demonstrate a substantial speedup compared to classical methods. We explore the core mechanism of leveraging superposition and entanglement to navigate the solution space and identify optimal solutions. The research focuses on a novel quantum algorithm designed to accelerate CSP solving, with the goal of providing a practical and efficient solution to this computationally intensive field. This work will detail the theoretical framework, implementation details, and preliminary results demonstrating the potential of quantum computing for CSP problems.

title: Relational Tensor Decomposition for Knowledge Graph Completion
abstract: Knowledge graphs (KGs) represent complex relationships between entities, offering a powerful means for reasoning and knowledge discovery. However, KGs are often incomplete, posing a significant challenge for tasks like link prediction – determining missing relationships. Traditional methods for link prediction, such as matrix factorization, struggle to effectively capture the high-order, relational structure inherent in KGs. This paper introduces a novel approach utilizing relational tensor decomposition. We represent a KG as a high-order tensor, where the tensor indices encode the relationships between entities. By applying tensor decomposition techniques, primarily Tucker decomposition, we can decompose this tensor to reveal latent factors representing the underlying relationships, enabling accurate prediction of missing links. The proposed method demonstrates improved accuracy and scalability compared to existing matrix factorization approaches, offering a promising direction for KG completion. Our key contribution lies in the explicit modeling of relationships within the tensor representation, leading to a more robust and accurate inference process.

title: Adaptive Metric Regularization for Machine Learning
abstract: This paper proposes an adaptive metric regularization technique for machine learning models, aiming to enhance model generalization and robustness through dynamic parameter adjustment based on the model's internal representation of the data. We introduce a neural network to assess the model's data representation, iteratively adjusting regularization strength to achieve optimal performance. The core mechanism centers around a self-regulating process where the network learns to prioritize data features that contribute most to model uncertainty, thereby mitigating overfitting and promoting better generalization. This approach offers a novel and automated method for optimizing model regularization, bypassing the limitations of traditional techniques. We present a framework demonstrating significant improvements in various benchmark datasets, highlighting the potential for widespread adoption in machine learning applications.

title: 非线性几何拓扑结构与量子纠缠的关联
abstract: This paper investigates the intricate relationship between non-linear geometric topology structures and quantum entanglement. We explore the potential for a profound connection between these two fields, hypothesizing that the inherent properties of non-linear geometry can fundamentally influence the dynamics of quantum entanglement. Specifically, we introduce a novel conceptual framework – the "quantum hidden matrix" – that leverages topological structure as the basis for quantum state representation. The paper outlines a computational model designed to analyze and simulate this connection, proposing that the unique characteristics of non-linear geometry might enhance or even modify quantum entanglement's observable behavior. The exploration of this connection suggests a potential paradigm shift in quantum information processing, moving beyond classical approaches reliant on precise state representations. We analyze the implications of this research for quantum cryptography and fundamental physics.

title: Dynamic Probability Field (DPF) – Adaptive Geometric Transformations
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Dynamic Probability Field (DPF) that allows for adaptive geometric transformations during computation. The primary goal is to achieve more efficient and flexible numerical simulations, and to automatically adapt to variations arising from different problem scenarios. The core of our approach lies in the development of a dynamic geometric transformation mechanism, driven by gradients or noise, that adjusts the geometric structure of variables based on the problem itself. Traditional DPFs primarily focus on static geometric transformations, while this work addresses the need for adaptive geometric changes. We present a detailed mathematical framework demonstrating this adaptation capability, highlighting its potential to significantly improve numerical methods for complex problems.

title: Dynamic Quantum State Superposition Generator (DQOSG)
abstract: This paper introduces the Dynamic Quantum State Superposition Generator (DQOSG), a novel approach to efficiently generating and manipulating quantum state superposition. Addressing limitations within conventional quantum computing superposition generation techniques, the DQOSG leverages precisely controlled microwave pulses interacting with superconducting circuits or ion traps to dynamically produce and manage superposition states. The core mechanism involves the manipulation of quantum bits (qubits) through the accurate control of their interactions, enabling dynamic superposition generation and control. This method represents a significant advancement, offering a pathway to scale quantum computing by providing a new state superposition generation method. The design principles and theoretical framework are presented, aiming to provide a foundational understanding for future research and development in this field. Specifically, the paper details the control architecture, pulse shaping strategies, and potential applications of the DQOSG. The design focuses on achieving high fidelity superposition generation and demonstrating scalability through modular architecture.

title: Causal Representation Learning for Creative Clusters Districts Systems in Kenya: Out-of-Distribution Benchmarking and Error Analysis
abstract: Creative clusters and districts in Kenya increasingly depend on computational systems whose predictions must remain reliable when the statistical context shifts. We define a generative model in which high-dimensional observations are governed by latent causal variables, some of which are invariant across environments and others of which are spuriously correlated with the target. The central contribution is a set of identifiability conditions under which an encoder can recover the invariant sub-representation, together with a decomposition of generalisation error into causal, spurious, and irreducible components. We prove that without an environment intervention on the target mechanism, no learner can distinguish invariant from spurious features, and we derive a sample-complexity bound for the proposed benchmarking protocol. The error analysis distinguishes three failure modes: attribute confounding, mechanism shift, and selection on spurious correlation. The framework is positioned as a methodological foundation for evaluating creative-cluster systems in Kenya, where data are scarce and distributional shifts are common, and it clarifies why purely correlational baselines are insufficient for reliable deployment.

title: cmc-tagger: A tagger for computer-mediated communication corpora
abstract: This poster presents cmc-tagger, an open-source, language-independent CoNLL-U tagger for computer-mediated communication (CMC) corpora. Extending the EmpiriST 2015 category inventory, it annotates emojis, ASCII emoticons, Wikipedia emoji templates, action words, hashtags, URLs, email and @-addresses in the XPOS column and, for Unicode emoji, enriches the FEATS column with metadata such as group, subgroup, qualification status, first emoji version, and normalized emoji name. Implemented as a fast Unix-style filter, it can be used standalone or integrated into larger annotation chains with minimal overhead. The tool is already applied to CMC corpora provided via the corpus analysis platform KorAP, where its annotations can be queried in combination with other annotation layers.

title: Algebraic width certificates guarantee interval type-2 fuzzy aggregation in multicriteria decision making
abstract: Abstract Interval type-2 (IT2) fuzzy multi-criteria decision systems have lacked a definitive answer to whether output uncertainty grows without bound as criteria accumulate—a gap that limits trust in clinical and industrial deployments. We prove that weight normalisation ( $$\sum _i w_i = 1$$ ) is the exact structural condition separating the two regimes: normalised aggregation yields an O(1) width certificate, while unnormalised aggregation forces $$\Omega (n)$$ growth. We derive closed-form certificates for sigmoid and triangular membership functions, Mamdani inference, cascaded pipelines, autoregressive inputs, multi-class decision margins, and concentration-based confidence bands, and validate them on five datasets spanning cardiac risk, diabetes scoring, and steel-plate fault detection. The certificates are tight (tightness ratio 0.51–0.97) and computed over $$400\times$$ faster than Monte Carlo simulation. The results close a question posed by Celik et al. [1] and give practitioners both a guarantee and a deployable algorithm for IT2 multi-criteria decision support.

title: When Semantically Consistent Encoding Meets View-Label Heterogeneity Modeling: A Unified Framework for Incomplete Multi-View Multi-Label Learning
abstract: Incomplete multi-view multi-label learning requires not only robust semantic aggregation from partially observed views, but also label-aware exploitation of view-specific evidence. Existing approaches usually emphasize either shared representation learning or decision-level fusion. The former improves robustness against missing views, yet tends to compress label-discriminative view-specific cues into a single latent representation. The latter preserves individual view predictions, but often relies on fixed or globally learned fusion weights, ignoring that different labels of different instances may require different views. To address these limitations, this paper presents V2L, a unified representation-decision framework for incomplete multi-view multi-label classification. On the representation side, V2L constructs semantically consistent variational posteriors from incomplete views through a perturbation-aware encoding mechanism, which provides a stable shared semantic basis. On the decision side, V2L introduces an active view-label relevance modeling strategy that estimates instance-wise and label-wise view contributions, allowing each label prediction to adaptively select useful view-specific evidence. From the perspective of model architecture, these two important strategies are integrated into a unified framework through a hybrid fusion architecture, simultaneously meeting the requirements of cross-view semantic consistency and representational complementarity. Extensive experiments under both incomplete and complete settings show that V2L achieves leading performance on five benchmarks. Code is available at: https://github.com/justsmart/V2L.

title: Recompilation Is Not Enough: Test-Guided Decompiled-C Repair
abstract: Decompiled C often becomes recompilable only after repair, but recompilation alone does not establish test-observed behavior. A recompiled command-line binary can still parse options incorrectly, print different bytes, or return a different exit status. We present a few-step workflow for repairing decompiled C using compiler feedback and related official tests. Compiler and linker diagnostics first guide build repair. Once the repaired C recompiles into a binary, smoke checks and related official tests expose behavioral discrepancies for semantic repair. In a preliminary static-enriched evaluation on 104 Coreutils 9.5 binaries with available decompiler exports and deterministic exact-output smoke comparisons, 91 binaries (87.5%) recompile and pass the test gate; 9 do not recompile within the repair budget, and 4 recompile but still fail the test gate. The result suggests that test-gate feedback can make LLM-assisted repair of decompiled C more auditable than compile-only recovery.

title: Quantum Machine Learning for Non-Linear Pattern Recognition
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) represents a paradigm shift in computational approaches, offering the potential to surpass classical machine learning algorithms in complex data analysis. This paper investigates the application of QML to the identification of non-linear patterns, focusing on leveraging quantum states to uncover hidden correlations and anomalies within datasets. We propose a novel framework that utilizes quantum entanglement and superposition to enhance pattern recognition capabilities. The core mechanism centers on harnessing the inherent properties of quantum states to provide a fundamentally different approach to data analysis, specifically designed to address the challenges posed by non-linear data. This research explores the potential of quantum algorithms to improve pattern detection and anomaly detection, and investigates the influence of quantum characteristics on pattern recognition processes. The paper will detail the implementation of a quantum model for pattern recognition, discuss its performance compared to classical models, and explore the fundamental principles underpinning its effectiveness. We argue that this work introduces a new perspective on pattern recognition, offering the possibility of enhanced accuracy, robustness, and the ability to identify subtle patterns within complex datasets. The core claim posits that quantum machine learning can effectively identify and interpret non-linear patterns, offering significant advantages over conventional methods.

abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum topology as a novel algorithmic framework for optimization. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with complex, high-dimensional problems, while quantum topology offers a unique geometric approach to search and solution. We propose a new algorithm, termed "Quantum Topology Optimization," which leverages quantum superposition and entanglement to identify and refine optimal parameter configurations for various applications, including machine learning and chemical reaction path optimization. The core mechanism involves constructing a quantum state representation that captures the inherent topological structure of the problem domain, enabling efficient exploration of the solution space and the identification of global optima. The algorithm demonstrates promising results across several benchmark problems, highlighting the potential of quantum topology to surpass conventional optimization techniques.

title: Dynamic Adaptive Machine Learning Loss Function Adjustment
abstract: Dynamic Adaptive Machine Learning Loss Function Adjustment is a novel approach to machine learning model training that dynamically adjusts the loss function coefficients to better adapt to changing data distributions. This paper introduces a framework utilizing a simulated data distribution change to optimize the loss function's sensitivity, leading to improved model performance and robustness. We present a method for generating synthetic data distributions, incorporating them into the loss function calculation, and evaluating the resulting model's generalization capabilities. The core mechanism involves a continuous, adaptive adjustment of the loss function coefficients based on a dynamically generated data distribution. This approach addresses the limitations of static loss function adjustments, offering a more flexible and potentially more effective training strategy.

title: TurnShift: Sequential Detection of Mid-Conversation Author Substitution via Behavioral User Profiling
abstract: Large language models deployed in conversational systems face a class of threats that content-based safety mechanisms cannot adequately address: multi-turn request sequences that appear benign in isolation yet pursue account takeover, credential harvesting, or social engineering when aggregated across a user's interaction history. TurnShift adapts UEBA-style behavioral profiling (EMA embedding centroids, online linguistic statistics, temporal patterns) to conversational-LLM anomaly detection, with emphasis on sequential detection. A first-pass per-message evaluation looked strong (F1 up to 0.794) but collapsed to F1 = 0.008 at realistic anomaly prevalence (0.29%) — a base-rate artifact diagnosed and analyzed in the paper. title: 基于拓扑量子计算的容错编码设计
abstract: This paper explores the design of a fault-tolerant encoding scheme specifically tailored for topological quantum computing. The central premise is to leverage the inherent robustness of topological protection against decoherence, a primary challenge in realizing practical quantum computers. We propose a scheme utilizing non-Abelian anyons, exotic quasiparticles found in topological superconductors, to construct a robust quantum code. The core concept involves encoding quantum information within the braiding operations of these anyons, where the resulting topological transformations inherently protect against local errors. The scheme's efficacy relies on the topological protection mechanism, effectively mitigating errors arising from environmental noise and imperfections in qubit control. This work provides a theoretical foundation for utilizing topological quantum computing to achieve high-fidelity quantum computation. The key mathematical elements explored include qubit states, braiding operations, and the mathematical description of the topological protection effect.

title: Bayesian Predictive Geometry for Optimal Algorithm Design
abstract: This paper introduces Bayesian Predictive Geometry (BPG) as a novel approach to algorithm design, aiming to automate the discovery of optimal search spaces. We propose a Bayesian neural network that learns a "geometry" of the search space based on algorithm constraints and desired outcomes, enabling adaptive exploration and optimization. The core mechanism utilizes a probabilistic framework to guide the search, leveraging Bayesian inference to refine the search space towards solutions that maximize performance metrics. The benefits of BPG include automated optimization, reduced manual effort, and the potential for discovering novel and unexpected algorithm designs. We present a preliminary implementation demonstrating the effectiveness of BPG in a specific, albeit simplified, algorithm design scenario.

title: Dynamic Geometric Transformations – Quantum Hidden Matrix Theory (QGHM)
abstract: This paper presents a novel optimization algorithm, Quantum Hidden Matrix Theory (QGHM), based on dynamic geometric transformations. We introduce a probabilistic approach to parameter optimization for complex physical systems, leveraging the inherent evolution of geometric structures to enhance the reliability of optimization results. The core mechanism involves dynamically adjusting the probability distribution of geometric entities, simulating system dynamics and utilizing topology for efficient optimization. This work addresses the limitations of traditional optimization methods by incorporating probabilistic modeling and topology. We demonstrate the effectiveness of QGHM through a series of simulations and preliminary analysis, showcasing its potential for improving the robustness and accuracy of optimization tasks.

title: Dynamically Weighted Graph Convolution with Attention-Based Resonance
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to graph convolutional learning, termed Dynamically Weighted Graph Convolution with Attention-Based Resonance. The core idea is to enhance traditional graph convolutional layers by incorporating a dynamically weighted connection scheme driven by an attention mechanism. This mechanism identifies and amplifies resonant patterns within the graph structure, leading to more efficient and adaptive learning. We propose a graph convolutional layer where each connection's weight is determined by an attention score reflecting the similarity between the node embeddings involved. This approach allows the model to prioritize relevant connections, effectively filtering out noise and focusing on the most informative relationships within the graph. The resulting architecture demonstrates improved performance in scenarios where resonant patterns are prevalent, showcasing the potential of this dynamically weighted approach for a variety of graph-based learning tasks. The key contribution lies in the integration of attention mechanisms within the graph convolution framework, providing a flexible and powerful tool for capturing complex graph structures.

title: Proof-Carrying Cryptography for Distributed Machine Learning
abstract: This paper addresses the limitations of current proof-carrying cryptography (PCC) implementations in the context of large-scale distributed machine learning (DLM). Traditional PCC approaches introduce significant overhead due to the need for proof generation and verification at every aggregation step, hindering the scalability of DLM systems. We propose a novel PCC protocol designed specifically for DLM aggregation, capitalizing on succinct non-interactive proofs (SNIPs) to minimize proof size and verification time. The protocol utilizes layered proofs and homomorphic encryption techniques to achieve enhanced efficiency. This work represents a significant adaptation of PCC principles to the specific requirements of DLM, aiming to overcome existing scalability bottlenecks and pave the way for more practical and efficient distributed learning deployments. The core contribution lies in the tailored design of a PCC protocol that effectively addresses the unique challenges posed by the aggregation process in DLM, offering a potential solution to the current limitations of PCC.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning with Dynamic Rule Extraction
abstract: This paper proposes a novel neuro-symbolic reasoning framework centered around dynamic rule extraction. The core idea is to combine the strengths of deep learning and symbolic reasoning, enabling a system to learn and refine symbolic rules directly from raw sensory data. Unlike traditional approaches that rely on pre-defined rules, our system utilizes a deep neural network to initially propose candidate rules, followed by a symbolic reasoning engine for validation and refinement. Crucially, the neural network continuously learns from the feedback provided by the reasoning engine, resulting in an adaptive and robust reasoning capability. We formalize this process with a dynamic rule extraction model, denoted as: Rt = fNR(St, Θt) Where: * Rt represents the set of rules extracted at time step *t*. * St denotes the sensory data observed at time step *t*. * Θt represents the parameters of the neural network at time step *t*. * fNR is the non-linear function representing the rule extraction process. The system iteratively updates its rule base, leading to enhanced performance in reasoning tasks. The framework is designed to address the limitations of both purely data-driven and purely symbolic approaches, offering a more flexible and adaptable solution for complex reasoning problems. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through a conceptual framework and highlight key considerations for its implementation, focusing on the interplay between the neural network and the symbolic engine. ---

title: Quantum-Enhanced Constraint Satisfaction (QCS) for Scheduling
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum-enhanced constraint satisfaction (QCS) algorithm, Quantum-Enhanced Constraint Satisfaction (QCS), designed to address the limitations of traditional constraint satisfaction methods when confronted with complex scheduling challenges. We propose a quantum annealing approach to efficiently explore the search space of possible schedules, potentially leading to optimal solutions for resource allocation problems. The core mechanism centers around utilizing quantum annealing to navigate the vast solution space, enabling faster and more effective scheduling outcomes. The paper details the algorithm's design, the rationale behind its quantum-enhanced nature, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating its potential for improved scheduling performance. We conclude with a discussion of future research directions, including exploration of scalability and optimization of the quantum annealing process.

title: Self-Adaptive Quantum Topology for Computational Geometry Optimization
abstract: Quantum topology offers a fundamentally different approach to geometric optimization compared to classical methods, leveraging the unique properties of quantum systems. This paper introduces a novel computational geometry optimization framework predicated on self-adaptive quantum topology, aiming to accelerate the solution of complex geometric optimization problems, particularly within the realms of machine learning and optimization algorithms. We propose a new approach that exploits the inherent topological properties of quantum states to achieve efficient and robust solutions. This framework provides a computationally-advantageous method for tackling intricate geometric challenges. The core mechanism centers around leveraging quantum tunneling and superposition to explore the solution space more effectively, reducing computational cost and improving overall performance. This work presents a significant advancement in the field of computational geometry optimization, demonstrating the potential of quantum topology to revolutionize the design and execution of complex geometric algorithms.

title: Contextualized Kolmogorov Complexity for Program Verification
abstract: Traditional program verification techniques predominantly rely on static analysis, which inherently struggles to accurately represent and quantify the inherent uncertainty present in the execution of programs. This paper proposes a novel approach to program verification by formalizing Kolmogorov complexity, specifically contextualized within the program's environment. The core idea is to define a "contextual Kolmogorov complexity" that incorporates the program's state, the input it receives, and its execution history. This allows for a more granular and meaningful assessment of a program's unpredictability. The framework outlines a method for formally proving program properties based on established complexity thresholds. The application of Kolmogorov complexity directly to program verification offers a potentially powerful alternative to existing techniques, providing a more robust measure of program behavior and facilitating the verification of systems with inherent probabilistic or randomized elements. This approach aims to bridge the gap between theoretical complexity theory and practical program verification.
